Jayhawk basketball is as rich in tradition and committed to winning championships as any program in the country. So why turn down Kansas men's basketball coach Bill Self if he offers you a scholarship?}} is a Bahamian [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|University of Oklahoma]]. He was named the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] in 2015 and 2016,{{cite web|title=Buddy Hield Biography|url=http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208409509|website=''SoonerSports.com''|accessdate=12 March 2015}} and in 2016 he received four major national player of the year awards—the [[John R. Wooden Award]], the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]], [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' Player of the Year]], and the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]]. ==Early life== Hield grew up in Eight Mile Rock, a coastal village 14 miles west of [[Freeport, Bahamas|Freeport]], in the [[West Grand Bahama]] district in [[The Bahamas]].Hield, Buddy. [http://www.theplayerstribune.com/buddy-hield-oklahoma-sooners-basketball/], The Players Tribune, March 17, 2016. He was fifth of seven children of his mother Jackie Braynen.{{cite news |last=Tracy |first=Marc |date=March 14, 2016 |title=For Buddy Hield and Other Bahamians, Talent Is Cultivated on the Great Plains |url=http://www.nytimes.com/2016/03/14/sports/ncaabasketball/sunrise-christian-academy-bahamas-buddy-hield.html?_r=0 |newspaper=New York Times |location=[[New York]] |access-date=April 12, 2016}} Hield received his nickname from his mother after [[Bud Bundy]] of the sitcom ''[[Married... with Children]]''.{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Vecenie |title=Oklahoma's Buddy Hield fueled by his roots of growing up in Bahamas |date=August 13, 2015 |work=CBS Sports |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25267076/oklahomas-buddy-hield-fueled-by-his-bahamian-roots }} Hield was first featured in high school by ''The All Bahamian Brand'', a basketball magazine from the Bahamas. Hield, as a young eighth grader, was rated by the All Bahamian Brand as the best 8th grader in the Bahamas and one to watch. Hield showed his early ability to lead his team from a young age by taking his Jack Hayward High School basketball team to the championship of the Providence Holiday Tournament on a buzzer beater and also leading his team to win the Grand Bahamas High School Championships. For his exploits, Hield was named an All Bahamian Brand All Bahamian Selection.{{Citation|title = SportsMEDIAoNe2009-2010allBahamianTeamVideo.mov|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Dcq00aRWxM&feature=youtu.be|date = 2010-08-26|accessdate = 2016-02-06|last = SportsMEDIAoNe1}} After his performances in The Bahamas, Hield was recruited to attend a prep school in Kansas, Sunrise Christian Academy in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]], a suburb of [[Wichita, Kansas|Wichita]]. Current [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] assistant and then-Sunrise coach Kyle Lindsted recruited the 6-foot 4-inch (1.93 m) guard. In 2011, during Hield's junior year at Sunrise Christian he lead the team to the National Association of Christian Athletes national championship, getting named the MVP of the tourney.{{cite news |last=King |first=Jason |date=November 19, 2015 |title=Bahamas' Best: Buddy Hield's Relentless Journey to Oklahoma and Hoops Stardom |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2590353-bahamas-best-buddy-hields-relentless-journey-to-oklahoma-and-hoops-stardom |newspaper=[[Bleacher Report]] |location=[[San Francisco]] |access-date=April 6, 2016 |quote=As the 86th-ranked player in the 2012 class by Rivals.com, Hield had been offered a scholarship by tradition-rich Kansas prior to his senior season. But he canceled his official visit and committed to Oklahoma following a trip to Norman, where Kruger had been hired to resurrect a dormant program.}} In the 2011-2012 season, his senior year, Hield averaged 22.7 points on .491 shooting in 21.0 minutes per game. He was highly recruited and selected the Oklahoma Sooners over the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]].{{cite news|last1=Rexrode|first1=Joe|title=MSU's Nairn, OU's Hield represent Bahamas, friendship|url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2015/03/25/michigan-state-spartans-oklahoma-tum-tum-nairn-buddy-hield/70469788/|accessdate=24 June 2015|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=25 March 2015}}Dodd, Rustin. [http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article52858315.html As No. 1 vs. No. 2 showdown looms, Kansas guards prepare for matchup with Oklahoma’s Buddy Hield], ''[[Kansas City Star]]'', January 3, 2016. "A native of the Bahamas, Hield, a 6-foot-4 shooting guard, had gone to Sunrise to pursue a college basketball scholarship, and after two seasons in Kansas, he was a top-100 recruit with offers from schools all over the country. One of those schools was KU. The Jayhawks’ staff was interested in Hield, Self says."{{cite news |last=Robinett |first=Kellis |date=February 4, 2016 |title=High school stop in Wichita gave OU’s Buddy Hield a path to success |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/article58483728.html#storylink=cpy |newspaper=[[Kansas City Star]] |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=April 8, 2016 }} ==College career== As a freshman at Oklahoma, Hield scored 7.8 points per game, and was the recipient of the team's Most Inspirational Award. He was a second-team All-Big 12 selection as a sophomore as he averaged 16.5 points and 4.4 rebounds per game. He worked on his defense prior to his junior year and expanded his offensive game to more of a high-volume [[Three-point field goal|three point shooter]].{{cite news|last1=Olson|first1=Eric|title=Oklahoma’s Buddy Hield thrives in the clutch|url=http://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2015/03/25/oklahomas-buddy-hield-thrives-clutch/70466904/|accessdate=24 June 2015|work=[[The Detroit News]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=25 March 2015}} Hield averaged 17.4 points and 5.4 rebounds per game as a junior at Oklahoma and shot 41 percent from the field. He led Oklahoma to a 24-11 record and Sweet 16 berth. Despite being a potential [[2015 NBA Draft]] selection, he decided to return for his senior season.{{cite news|title=Big 12 Player of Year Hield returning to Oklahoma for senior season|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-returning-senior-season-no-nba-042415|accessdate=25 April 2015|work=[[Fox Sports]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=24 April 2015}} He was a First Team All-Big 12 selection and was named [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Sooners' Hield Leads All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Honors|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209934691|website=[[Big 12 Conference]]|accessdate=May 17, 2015|date=March 8, 2015}} Hield was listed on the [[Oscar Robertson Award]] preseason watchlist{{cite web|title=USBWA Unveils Award Watchlists|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2016/watchlists151202.html|website=[[U.S. Basketball Writers Association]]|accessdate=December 22, 2015}} as well as the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] preseason watchlist.{{cite web|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2015/12/02/naismith-trophy-early-season-watch-list-released/|title=Naismith Trophy early season watch list released|accessdate=December 3, 2015|date=December 2, 2015|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|author=Johnson, Raphielle}} Hield recorded a career high of 46 points in a triple overtime loss to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] on January 4, 2016, receiving a standing ovation from the opposing crowd after a postgame interview with Scott Van Pelt. His 46 points tied the record for most points scored by an opponent at [[Allen Fieldhouse]].{{cite news|last1=Mattioli|first1=Kami|title=Kansas fans stick around to show love for Oklahoma's Buddy Hield|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball-news/4690175-kansas-fans-stick-around-to-show-love-for-oklahomas-buddy-hield|accessdate=January 6, 2016|work=[[The Sporting News]]|date=January 5, 2016}} He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the Naismith Trophy on February 11.{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|accessdate=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}} His senior year at Oklahoma, on April 7, 2016, Hield won the [[John R. Wooden Award]] for the best college basketball player for the 2015-2016 season; where he averaged 25 points, 5.7 rebounds, two assists per game, and led the nation in three-point shots.{{cite news |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |date=April 8, 2016 |title=Oklahoma's Buddy Hield named 2016 Wooden Award winner |url=http://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2016/4/8/11396004/buddy-hield-named-2016-wooden-award-winner-oklahoma |newspaper=[[SB Nation]] |location=[[New York City]] |access-date=April 13, 2016}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]] || [[2012–13 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team |Oklahoma]] || 27 || 13 || 25.1 || .388 || .238 || .833 || 4.2 || 1.9 || 1.2 || .3 || 7.8 |- | [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14]] || [[2013–14 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team |Oklahoma]] || 33 || 33 || 32.1 || .445 || .386 || .750 || 4.4 || 1.9 || '''1.4''' || .2 || 16.5 |- | [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15]] || [[2014–15 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team |Oklahoma]] || 35 || 35 || 32.4 || .412 || .359 || .823 || 5.4 || 1.9 || 1.3 || .2 || 17.4 |- | [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16]] || [[2015–16 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team |Oklahoma]] || '''37''' || '''37''' || '''35.4''' || '''.501''' || '''.457''' || '''.880''' || '''5.7''' || '''2.0''' || 1.1 || '''.5''' || '''25.0''' |- class="sortbottom" | Career|| ||132|| 118 || 31.7 || .448 || .390 || .836 || 5.0 || 1.9 || 1.3 || .3 || 17.4 |} ==International career== Hield traveled to the city of [[Tepic]] in [[Nayarit]], [[Mexico]] from August 1 to 7, 2014 to represent the [[Bahamas national basketball team|Bahamas national team]] in the 2014 [[Centrobasket]], which is the regional [[basketball]] championship of [[FIBA Americas]] for the [[Central America|Central American]] and [[Caribbean]] subzone. Hield's coach in the tournament was [[Larry Eustachy]]. He averaged a tournament-leading 19.8 points per game and a team-high 6.0 rebounds.{{cite news |last=Rohde |first=John |date=August 28, 2014 |title=The Summer of Buddy Love |url=http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=31000&ATCLID=209621669&SPID=127260&SPSID=750395 |newspaper=SoonerSports.com |location=[[Norman, Oklahoma]] |access-date=April 8, 2016 |quote=Playing four games in the city of Tepic in the western part of the country for former Iowa State and current Colorado State head coach Larry Eustachy, Hield averaged a tournament-leading 19.8 points per game and a team-high 6.0 rebounds.}} ==See also== * [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season 3-point field goal leaders]] ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== * [http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208409509 Oklahoma Sooners bio] {{Navboxes|list1= {{Wooden Player of the Year men}} {{Naismith Player of the Year men}} {{Sporting News College Men's Basketball Player of the Year}} {{Oscar Robertson Trophy}} {{2016 NCAA Men's Basketball Consensus All-Americans}} {{Jerry West Award}} {{Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Hield, Buddy}} [[Category:1993 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Bahamian basketball players]] [[Category:Bahamian Christians]] [[Category:Bahamian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Freeport, Bahamas]] [[Category:People from West Grand Bahama]] [[Category:Shooting guards]]
